title: Feature: CLI
body:
This PR implements the CLI as described in the approved design documentation. The CLI is the endpoint of the remote job execution service, providing users with a simple UX for starting, stopping, monitoring, and streaming output from jobs.

The README and Makefile have been updated to support the CLI and `jobctl` binary.

Key Details:
- `--cert` flag allows users to run commands as admin, user, or unknown client
- Unique job ID's are output for every new job started, allowing an easy means of interacting with each new job.

---

Usage:

`./bin/linuxjobctl <cmd> <args>`

By utilizing this path, the CLI maintains access to the certificates in `certs`. This is currently the method best utilizes for interacting with the CLI tool

title: Feature: Client API
body:
This PR implements the Client portion of the API as described in the approved design documentation. The gRPC client is the entry point for the end-user's CLI tool. It manages the mTLS handshake, credential loading, and the lifecycle of long-lived gRPC streams, ensuring secure and resilient communication with the remote service.

Key Details:
- mTLS authentication (TLS 1.3 enforced) for all outgoing requests. The client automatically manages certificate loading and verifies server identity against a trusted CA
- Resilient stream management, including managing the lifecycle of long-lived gRPC streams for job output

Updates to the README have been made to reflect the core components of the Client implementation.

---

Current testing coverage for the Worker Library is **77.3%**, and is `-race` compliant.

Key scenarios tested:
- Non-existent job interactions
- Client response to no server
- Multi-client output streaming

title: Feature: Server API
body:
This PR implements the Server portion of the API as described in the approved design documentation. This includes the service’s core functionality for security, including RBAC authorization and mTLS authentication. The Server also implements the RPCs, and connects the service's key functionality to the Worker library

Key Details:
- mTLS authentication (TLS 1.3 enforced)
- RBAC authorization (SAN identity-driven)
- Thread-safe RPC implementation including `StartJob`, `StopJob`, `GetStatus`, and `StreamOutput`

Additional Details:

Updates to the README have been made to reflect the core components of the Server implementation. The Makefile has been updated for the Server.

---

Current testing coverage for the Worker Library is **73.1%**, and is `-race` compliant.

Key scenarios tested:
- RPCs are limited based on user role
- TLS enforced
- Context cancellation of streams, not jobs
- Streaming live and historical output

title: Feature: Worker Library
body:
This PR implements the Worker Library as described in the approved design documentation. This includes the service’s core functionality as it pertains to job tracking and lifecycle management, output streaming, and concurrency support for multiple clients.

**Key Details**:
- Raw byte streaming with on-disk log files allows for complete historical and live output streaming
- POSIX guarantees are leveraged to ensure all readers are able to access new data when output is written to disk
- Broker’s support for `io.Writer` allows both stdout and stderr to be merged into a single, serialized writer.
- `sync.Cond` is utilized to support multiple concurrent readers without polling or busy waiting.

**Additional Details**:
- Updates to the README have been made to reflect the core components of the Worker Library 
- A Makefile has been included. This allows for ease of use when running tests, as well as executing common commands necessary for the project.
- Current testing coverage for the Worker Library is **87.4%**, and is `-race` compliant.

---

**Note**: for the sake of completeness, I have included both the complete set of certificates used for the challenge at present, as well as the script used to generate them. In this way, you can either clone the repo and generate your own scripts or use those provided here. 

In a production situation, certificates would never be included in a repo such as this.

title: Design Specification and .proto for the remote job execution service (L4 implementation)
body:
## Design Document

This PR includes the design documentation that outlines my plans for implementing the remote job execution service. It covers how I plan to handle job output streaming with `sync.Cond`, the gRPC API, mTLS authentication, and how user authorization is determined and enforced. 

## ProtoBuffer

The `.proto` file that outlines the gRPC API for the service has been included to show the core functionality of the API, including starting, stopping, monitoring, and streaming jobs.

## Next Steps
Once this design is approved, I will begin implementing the core Worker library, as described in the design doc.
